$comment: Lip sync v3 rules for lib/lipsync-v3.mjs (author's prompt #18): v2's letter rules (rig/lipsync-text.json as frozen in 3df3c97, copied here so v3 stands on its own) and three rules of v3. Labelled "changed after seeing P1 to P3 and H1 to H4". FROZEN with v3 (rig/frozen.json); the last version for this episode, only bugs get fixed.

changedAfterSeeing.label: changed after seeing P1 to P3 and H1 to H4
changedAfterSeeing.seen: P1-P3 and H1-H4 (author's prompt #18): the majority rule lost short closures (b in "Bob brought a big", p in "Open") and the minimum-run rule erased short vowels ("My", "am", "you").

closure.why: lips together (m, b, p) or upper teeth on the lip (f, v): on this face both read as the closed smile

gap.why: spaces, punctuation and time no letter covers: the mouth at rest

f.why: upper teeth on the lower lip; Ping has no teeth, so F and V map to rest (step 1 decision)

o.why: o is said with rounded lips

u.why: u is said with rounded lips

e.why: e is said with spread lips

i.why: i is said with spread lips

y.rule: consonant at the start of a word before a vowel (you, yes), vowel everywhere else (my, very)
y.why: y before a vowel at a word start is a glide; elsewhere it is said like i or ee

onlyVowel.rule: when y is the only vowel letter of a word (no a, e, i, o or u): my, by, why
onlyVowel.why: said like 'I', which opens the jaw
onlyVowel.changedAfterSeeing: the author's prompt #16, after reading out/lipsync-v2/words.txt: "My" came out wide; it sounds like "I".

otherLetters.why: other consonants: tongue and teeth, mouth a little open

pairs.why: tongue between the teeth: a little open, not wide
mouth, sound, loud, wow: the sound starts open and ends round, so the first letter is open and the second round
pairs.changedAfterSeeing: the author's prompt #16, after reading out/lipsync-v2/words.txt: "mouth", "sound", "loud", "wow" came out round only; the sound starts open.

pairs.why: mouth, sound, loud, wow: the sound starts open and ends round, so the first letter is open and the second round
pairs.changedAfterSeeing: the author's prompt #16, after reading out/lipsync-v2/words.txt: "mouth", "sound", "loud", "wow" came out round only; the sound starts open.

pairs.why: each, read: said as ee, not as a
back of the tongue, mouth a little open; not two shapes

silentFinalE.rule: a word that ends in a consonant followed by e and has three or more letters, other than words ending in ee and the exceptions
silentFinalE.exceptionsWhy: the final e is said in these short words; found by a unit test before anything was rendered
silentFinalE.why: move, live: the final e is not said, so it must not spread the lips

pronounI.why: said like 'eye', which opens the jaw before it spreads

priorityWhy: since prompt #17 only for exact ties: when letters of two classes fall in one frame, the higher one wins: closures and roundings are the shapes a viewer misses most when they are skipped, an open jaw next; small is the default; gaps lose to any letter

frameRule.rule: a frame takes the character that covers most of its time window; class priority only breaks exact ties; spaces, punctuation and time no character covers compete as gap (as v2 since prompt #17)

closureRescue.rule: every m, b, p, f or v whose class is closure and that won no frame takes the frame it overlaps most (on a tie the earlier frame), unless that frame already shows a closure
closureRescue.tieWhy: chosen by Claude: the author's rule names no tie; the earlier frame closes the lips no later than the letter starts
closureRescue.why: P1-P3 and H1-H4 (author's prompt #18): the majority rule lost short closures (b in "Bob brought a big", p in "Open") and the minimum-run rule erased short vowels ("My", "am", "you").

minFramesRule: a run shorter than minFrames first grows: it takes one frame from a neighbouring run that would still keep minFrames (the longer neighbour; on a tie the later one), one frame at a time. Only if neither neighbour can give a frame is it removed (it takes the class of the run before it, or after it at the start). A closure run is never removed; it may stay one frame long. Runs are checked from the start of the phrase, again after every change. Decided by Claude after a test on H2 ("brought" lost its b when a short small run grew into the closure run before it): rule 2 says a letter that ends up with no frame, so a closure frame that is the last closure frame overlapping an m, b, p, f or v cannot be given.
minFramesWhy: a mouth held for one frame at 30 fps reads as flicker; v2's removal also erased short vowels ("My", "am", "you"), so v3 grows a short run before it removes it
from: rig/lipsync-text.json (v2) as frozen in 3df3c97: letters, y, otherLetters, pairs, silentFinalE, pronounI, classes, priority and minFrames are the same values
